scene_purpose: Capture the first extraordinary moment: a silent, impossibly bright light over the distant forest.
main_subject: A white-blue atmospheric flash low over the horizon, dark pre-dawn taiga landscape in front, tiny cabin lights in the valley.

camera.angle: Wide shot from an elevated ridge, horizon in the upper third
camera.composition: Flash upper-left as the single luminous pole; dark conifer silhouettes frame left and right edges; valley floor catches faint rim light; strong negative space in the dark sky.

lighting.direction: Single intense point source near the horizon, upper-left
lighting.intensity_and_character: Extremely bright white-blue core with physically plausible atmospheric scattering halo; rims the nearest tree tops; the rest of the scene stays in deep cool shadow — no lightning bolts, no fantasy beams.

foreground_elements: dark ridge with moss and low shrubs
conifer silhouettes with faint blue rim light
environmental_details: detail retained in shadows (not crushed to black)
flash sits ABOVE the forest, not on the ground
animation_opportunities: flash intensity ramp 0->1 with shadow sweep
fog colour lerp toward blue-white (invert the s1 warm lerp)
must_preserve: enormous brightness contrast with soft roll-off, not clipped
can_simplify: halo to layered additive sprite billboards (glowTexture with cool stops)
valley detail to near-black geometry with one emissive cabin-window quad
mist to fog + one particles() layer

engine_mapping.flash: DirectionalLight '#cfe4ff' intensity ramp 0->8 driven in render(t); additive sprite stack via glowTexture([[0,'rgba(240,250,255,1)'],[0.3,'rgba(170,200,255,0.8)'],[1,'rgba(120,160,255,0)']])
engine_mapping.shadows: fireLight pattern from s1_dawn_fireball.js reused: castShadow DirectionalLight placed at flash position
engine_mapping.forest: standard makeForest; rely on rim light from the flash direction
engine_mapping.grade: keep project.json grade; raise bloom locally for this shot only if needed
